real_builder_surface_discovered.correction: The Phase L3 spec and the header comment both understate and overstate this. The header said 'Pass 1: BeginPlay, PrintString'; the pass specs in docs/superpowers/specs/ describe eleven passes including Delay, VariableGet/VariableSet, ForLoop and ForEachLoop. Reading the implementation, only the eight types above have dispatch cases in this repository. The forty-odd node factories in BPNodeRegistry.cpp belong to a different subsystem, UBlueprintMutatorLibrary::AddNode, which BuildBlueprintFromJSON does not call.
other_functions_on_the_library: SetComponentProperty (not fronted; see limitation 6 in CAPABILITY_FINDINGS)

design_decisions: Validate before mutate. BuildBlueprintFromJSON returns void and only warns about an unknown node type, so a bad spec would otherwise produce a Blueprint that compiles clean and does nothing. The native command validates the whole spec first: asset path, parent class, component classes, attach targets, node types, duplicate ids, and connection endpoints. Every check that does not need the asset runs before the asset is created, and the two that do need it only apply when it already exists, so a rejected request never creates or mutates anything.

GetSupportedNodeTypes() is the gate, not a parallel list. The node loop in BuildBlueprintFromJSON now checks it, so a dispatch case missing from the list stops working loudly instead of the list going quietly stale.

Idempotency by convergence rather than by no-op. The asset is loaded when it exists; a component whose name and class already match is left alone; the event graph is rebuilt from the spec because clear_existing_graph defaults to true. A rerun of the same spec reaches the same end state.
A conflicting rerun is an error, not a silent update. A different parent class, or a different class under a component name the Blueprint already uses, is rejected rather than reparented or renamed.

Assets are limited to /Game/MCPGenerated/, matching sky_shader_create. clear_existing_graph would otherwise let a caller wipe a hand-authored Blueprint's event graph anywhere in /Game. Widening this is a deliberate later decision, not a default.
Annotated destructiveIdempotent. It converges, but a build aimed at an existing Blueprint replaces its event graph, which a plain undo does not restore.

Per-tool client timeout. PuerTSClient had one 7 second ceiling for every command; asset authoring blocks the game thread for as long as Unreal needs to compile and save, and a client timeout while the editor is still working reports a failure for work that succeeds. Added an optional timeout argument, 30 s for blueprint_build. Measured cost turned out to be 91 ms, so the headroom is unused today.

The MCP schema publishes the node types as an enum. A client told 'any node type' writes graphs the builder skips. The native side re-validates, so the enum can only reject earlier, never let through a type the builder cannot build.

notes: The session's own MCP server process predates this build, so its tool list does not include puerts_blueprint_build. Acceptance was driven through the repo's freshly built mcp-server/dist/index.js over stdio, the same lane Scripts/puerts-live-smoke.mjs uses: same binary, same named pipe, same protocol as a real client. No second editor, no alternate transport. Restart the session to get the tool in the session catalog.

Every blueprint_build save logs 'Unable to Check Out From Source Control' as an auto-dismissed modal. The save succeeds; the test project has a source control provider configured that cannot reach its server. Worth knowing before someone reads it as a build failure.

puerts-runtime/typing/ue/ue.d.ts was not regenerated. It is an editor-toolbar snapshot documented in its PROVENANCE.md, already one commit behind after the serializer change, and the runtime compiles against the hand-written puerts-runtime/types/puerts-bootstrap.d.ts, which was updated.
